label: Bible Study
prompt: Put on the whole _____ of God, that ye may be able to stand against the wiles of the devil.
verse: Put on the whole armour of God, that ye may be able to stand against the wiles of the devil.
note: The whole armour — Paul itemizes the pieces a few verses later.

label: Warm-Up Word
prompt: Know therefore that the LORD thy God, he is God, the _____ God, which keepeth covenant and mercy with them that love him and keep his commandments to a thousand generations;
verse: Know therefore that the LORD thy God, he is God, the faithful God, which keepeth covenant and mercy with them that love him and keep his commandments to a thousand generations;
note: Covenant-keeping to a thousand generations — God's faithfulness has a very long memory.

label: Sunday School
prompt: And Ruth the Moabitess said unto Naomi, Let me now go to the field, and _____ ears of corn after him in whose sight I shall find grace. And she said unto her, Go, my daughter.
verse: And Ruth the Moabitess said unto Naomi, Let me now go to the field, and glean ears of corn after him in whose sight I shall find grace. And she said unto her, Go, my daughter.
note: Gleaning was Israel's welfare law — leftovers at the field's edge, where Ruth met Boaz.

label: Deep Water
prompt: For even when we were with you, this we commanded you, that if any would not _____, neither should he eat.
verse: For even when we were with you, this we commanded you, that if any would not work, neither should he eat.
note: Paul's blunt Thessalonian house rule — a correction for idlers, not for those who couldn't work.

label: Don't Play With Me
prompt: Now then we are _____ for Christ, as though God did beseech you by us: we pray you in Christ's stead, be ye reconciled to God.
verse: Now then we are ambassadors for Christ, as though God did beseech you by us: we pray you in Christ's stead, be ye reconciled to God.
note: 'Ambassadors for Christ' — the embassy metaphor every missions sermon borrows from this verse.
